task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a straight news update of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about Fenharbor's purchase of a creekside parking lot for a future floodwater-storage project. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 9, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Fenharbor Council voted 6-1 on Sept. 8, 2026, to buy the 2.4-acre Mill Bend parking lot.
The purchase price is $460,000, funded with $240,000 from a city reserve and a $220,000 regional land-acquisition grant.
The privately owned lot contains 87 marked parking spaces beside Narrow Creek, a short walk from the town's shopping streets.
The seller accepted the city's offer, but closing is scheduled for November and ownership has not yet transferred.
The city intends to remove pavement and create land that can hold water during high creek levels.
A design and environmental assessment must precede construction; the council vote purchases land rather than approving a final engineering plan.
The acquisition grant does not pay for demolition or construction, and neither expense has a confirmed funding allocation.
The city recorded flooding on the parking lot during storms in 2019 and 2024, but those records do not measure the proposed project's effect.
City engineer Hollis Vare said, "Buying room for water is the first step, not a promise that every nearby property will stay dry."
The current parking operator will continue running the lot until the sale closes under the terms described in the council report.
The council has not announced when parking will end after closing or when any public recreation area might open.
A merchants group says the lot is important to workers whose shifts begin before nearby short-stay spaces become available.
Merchants group chair Rima Doss said, "We support fixing the flooding, but the replacement for a workday parking space cannot be a two-hour space."
The city will examine converting six curb spaces to loading bays, a separate proposal that has not been approved.
An existing public path runs outside the purchase boundary and will remain under the parks department's management.
The draft concept includes a planted basin rather than a permanent pond, but plantings and public access arrangements remain undecided.
The dissenting council member wanted parking alternatives identified before the city committed the reserve money.
The regional grant requires the land to remain available for floodwater storage and does not permit later commercial development.
The assessment will include soil sampling because the parcel previously served as a vehicle storage yard.
The packet contains no finding that the soil is contaminated and no estimate of any cleanup expense.
The lot's old pay booth carries a painted fish emblem left by a former parking operator.
A public design meeting will be scheduled after the assessment contract is arranged; no meeting date has been published.

forbidden_additions: A completed sale, immediate parking closure or funded construction plan.
A guaranteed reduction in flooding or confirmed contaminated soil.
Approved replacement parking or loading bays.
preserve: Land acquisition distinguished from a final project and its funding.
The merchants' workday-parking concern rather than opposition to flood protection in general.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
